Filter scores and contamination summaries

Source: R/methods.R
filter_scores.Rd

filter_scores() returns the posterior probability \(s_j\) that each non-probability unit is compatible with the target model (the Rao-Blackwellised posterior mean of its latent indicator). Small values flag likely contaminated units. contamination() summarises the posterior of the contamination fraction \(1 - \pi\).

Usage

filter_scores(object, entropy = FALSE)

contamination(object, level = 0.95)

Arguments

object

A bsm_fit object.

entropy

If TRUE, return a data frame that also contains the binary entropy (nats) of each score, a measure of classification uncertainty (maximal, \(\log 2\), at \(s_j = 0.5\)).

level

Credible-interval level.

Value

filter_scores(): a numeric vector named by the rows of nonprob_data used in the fit, or a data frame if entropy = TRUE. contamination(): a named vector with posterior mean, median and credible limits of \(1 - \pi\).

Examples

d <- simulate_mixture_data("gaussian", n_prob = 100, n_nonprob = 100,
                           contamination = 0.3, seed = 6)
fit <- mixture_fit(y ~ x1, d$prob, d$nonprob, n_iter = 600, burnin = 200, seed = 1)
s <- filter_scores(fit)
tapply(s, d$nonprob$contaminated, mean)   # low scores for contaminated units
#>         0         1 
#> 0.9486064 0.2355229 
contamination(fit)
#>      mean    median     lower     upper 
#> 0.2690224 0.2678621 0.1862934 0.3651758
